problems.problem: The hard-days check (hardcheck.json, tone lens, severity should) found a rule 6 problem, and the batch still carries the old sentence. The context clause says the command is to fight ‘those who fight them’. The reading then says al-Tabari ‘takes the command as unrepealed’. Read together, the two leave him holding a standing command against attackers only. That is gentler than his own reading. After preferring ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz’s view that the ayah is not repealed, he paraphrases it in his own voice: the command is to fight the unbelievers’ fighting men (muqatilat ahl al-kufr) and not their women and children. So the line he draws is between combatants and non-combatants, and the sentence does not carry that scope. A revision was written that fixed it (revise/quran-01-d003-p.json). The refutation (revrefute/quran-01-d003-p.json) accepted its substance and objected only to the watch-list word ‘unbelievers’, but the corrected sentence it proposed never landed. The problem is still in the batch.
problems.fix: s = ‘The verse opens the ayahs commanding the believers to fight, slay and drive out those who fight them; al-Tabari, on 2:190, takes it as unrepealed, binding against the disbelievers’ fighting men, and reads the forbidden aggression as killing women, children or those who pay tribute.’ This is 45 words. ‘Disbelievers’ is Pickthall’s word in 2:191. The sentence passes entry-check with no warnings (scratch/c1-fix-3.json). The evidence is the revision’s three verbatim runs from packet.js quran 3 --verse 2.190. Key, ref, at, by and src are unchanged.
